NADIA BRENNAN-AZIZ
Senior Platform / Site Reliability Engineer
nadia.brennanaziz@example.com | +44 7700 900909 | github.com/nba-sre-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior platform and site reliability engineer with 10 years of infrastructure experience, including six years running Kubernetes platforms on AWS. Experienced in designing, building and operating cloud infrastructure, maintaining Terraform-based environments, and creating reliable, observable platforms that make it easier for product teams to deploy and operate services. Technical lead of a five-person platform team, with a record of improving delivery speed, reliability and infrastructure cost.

CORE SKILLS
Cloud infrastructure: AWS (EKS, EC2, VPC, IAM, RDS, S3, SQS, Route 53, CloudFront), Kubernetes, Linux
Infrastructure as code and automation: Terraform, Atlantis, Crossplane, Puppet, Bash, Python, Go
Platform engineering: Argo CD, Helm, Kustomize, GitHub Actions, internal developer platforms, service templates
Reliability and observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Alertmanager, OpenTelemetry, SLOs, error budgets, incident management
Performance and operations: k6, capacity planning, on-call operations

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Senior Platform Engineer | Tallybrook Ltd (B2B accounting SaaS) | Apr 2022–Present
- Technical lead of a five-person platform team operating an AWS EKS platform across eight clusters and three regions, supporting approximately 350 services.
- Built an internal developer platform with Go and Python service templates, Argo CD GitOps and Crossplane self-service for RDS, SQS and S3; adopted by all 14 product teams and reduced new-service production time from about two weeks to under one day.
- Led the migration from managed node groups to Karpenter, using spot instances for stateless workloads; reduced EC2 spend by 38% (about £410,000 per year).
- Introduced SLOs, burn-rate alerts and error-budget policies for the 20 most critical services, working with product leadership; reduced on-call pages by about 60%.
- Serve in the incident commander rotation and established the incident and post-mortem process.

Site Reliability Engineer | Brightwater Games | Jan 2019–Mar 2022
- Operated AWS infrastructure for game backends serving titles with up to 1.2 million daily active players, using EC2, ECS and EKS.
- Managed AWS infrastructure as code with approximately 40 Terraform modules and Atlantis pull-request plan/apply workflows.
- Replaced noisy Nagios alerting with a Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Loki observability stack.
- Load-tested a game launch with k6 simulations of 300,000 concurrent players, identifying and fixing a connection-pool limit before launch; also led launch capacity planning.

Linux Systems Engineer | Pennine Hosting | Jul 2016–Dec 2018
- Managed approximately 600 Linux servers for hosting customers using Puppet configuration management.
- Automated operational tasks with Bash and Python and provided on-call support for customer incidents.

SELECTED PROJECT
Kubernetes preview-namespace cleanup controller | Open-source side project | 2024
- Built a Go controller using controller-runtime to delete expired preview namespaces; the project has approximately 120 GitHub stars.

EDUCATION
BSc Computer Science | University of the North Moors | 2016

CERTIFICATIONS
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) | 2021; renewed 2024
AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional | 2023

ADDITIONAL
Speaker, UK DevOps meetup (2024): “SLOs that product managers care about”
Mentored three engineers transitioning from backend engineering into SRE
Languages: English (native), Urdu (conversational)
docs.cover_letter:
Dear Corvale Mobility hiring team,

I am applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor – Fleet Connectivity engagement. I bring 10 years of infrastructure experience, including six years operating Kubernetes platforms on AWS, and a strong track record of taking platform improvements from design through production.

At Tallybrook, I am the technical lead of a five-person platform team operating EKS across eight clusters and three regions. I built an internal developer platform using Terraform, Argo CD and Crossplane that all 14 product teams adopted, reducing the time to take a new service to production from about two weeks to under one day. I have also led infrastructure cost and reliability initiatives, including a Karpenter migration that reduced EC2 spend by 38% and an SLO programme that reduced on-call pages by about 60%. These projects required practical system decisions, clear operational standards and collaboration with product teams.

My production experience is in cloud platforms and backend services rather than train connectivity. I would bring relevant experience in AWS infrastructure design and operation, Terraform, Linux, observability and reliability as Corvale develops the cloud systems for its new train fleet. At Brightwater Games, I operated services supporting up to 1.2 million daily active players and used load testing and capacity planning to prepare for high-demand launches.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my platform and SRE experience could support Corvale’s fleet connectivity work, from infrastructure foundations through to reliable production services.

Best wishes,
Nadia Brennan-Aziz
